text:
Two goals in 89 seconds late in the third period turned a game Philadelphia was winning into one New York took. Pavel Dorofeyev tied it on the power play at 13:52, and Tye Kartye, a player nobody drafted who earned his NHL job as a free agent after a 28-goal AHL season at Coachella Valley, made it 3-2 at 15:21. Adam Fox assisted on both, and the Rangers closed it out at Madison Square Garden.

The Flyers had their moment in the second period. Simon Benoit scored on a shot we gave less than a 1% chance of going in, and Noel Acciari followed two minutes later to put PHI up 2-1. Philadelphia carried that period, out-chancing New York 1.40 expected goals to 0.97 (expected goals measure the quality of chances, not just the count of shots). But the Rangers had opened the scoring when Gabe Perreault deflected one in at 4:39 of the first, and they owned the third, 1.68 to 0.76 in chance quality.

Over the full game, our simulation of every shot says NYR deserved to win 57% of the time, so the result matched the play, if narrowly. Dylan Garand was a touch better than expected in the Rangers' net, and Joseph Woll gave Philadelphia roughly what the chances called for, neither goalie swinging it. The facts we have don't say where this leaves either club in the standings or on a streak, so we'll stop at the result: New York took the one that got away from them in the second, and Philadelphia let a one-goal lead slip in the last seven minutes.
